issues.failure_explanation: The Encode-Decode loss is presented as a J*J-weighted conditional-mean regression 'in a different geometry' from the unweighted Encode-Only CEM. But (i) for the paper's main choice rho=gamma the decoder is a translation, its Jacobian is the identity (so Algorithm alg:mf_training_encode_decode states), and eq:mf_loss_encode_decode therefore coincides with eq:mf_loss; no different geometry exists. (ii) Even for rho=rho_W, J(z_t) is an invertible function of the conditioning variable z_t, so the weighted and unweighted least-squares problems share the same population minimizer E[w_tgt | z_t,r,t,tilde y_obs]; the weighting cannot define a different estimator. (iii) 'benign for prior-aligned trace-class references' is contradicted by Table tab:encode-decode, where the anisotropic Encode-Decode model reports epsilon_sigma of 2.09e-1, 3.15e-1, 2.92e-1 versus 5.09e-2, 8.68e-2, 5.39e-2 for Encode-Only in Table tab:benchmark_summary.

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem thm:dimfree_lip_velocity is stated on the separable Hilbert space H set up in Appendix app:lipschitz_colored, but the paper's own remark concedes that the cited result is 'stated and proved in finite dimensions' and only offers that dimension-free constants let one 'interpret it as a function-space stability statement'. Dimension-uniform finite-dimensional bounds do not by themselves produce a Lipschitz velocity field on H: the object must first be shown to exist there and a limiting/transfer argument with uniform constants is required. No such argument is supplied, so the premise used by Lemma lem:avg_velocity_lipschitz, Corollary cor:exists_lipschitz_onestep and Theorem thm:lipschitz_onestep_main is unestablished in the stated scope.

issues.failure_explanation: w(\cdot;r,t) is the trajectory average (1/(t-r))\int_r^t v(z_tau,tau) dtau, so as a function of the endpoint z=z_t it equals (z-phi_{r,t}(z))/(t-r) with phi_{r,t} the flow map. Differentiating gives Dw=(1/(t-r))(I-D phi_{r,t}) with ||D phi_{r,t}|| bounded by exp(\int_r^t Lip(v(s,\cdot))ds); the asserted inequality bounds Lip(w(\cdot;r,t)) by the plain time average of Lip(v(tau,\cdot)) and drops these stretching factors entirely, and no proof is given beyond 'Assume Theorem ...'. Using only the stated hypothesis Lip(v(t,\cdot)) <= L_0 t, the field v(t,z)=tAz with ||A||=1 (L_0=1) yields Dw=(1/(t-r))(exp((t^2-r^2)A/2)-I), hence Lip(w(\cdot;0,1))=e^{1/2}-1 > 1/2 = L_0/2, contradicting the 'In particular' bound.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redo the estimate keeping the flow Jacobians (e.g. Lip(w(\cdot;r,t)) <= (1/(t-r))\int_r^t Lip(v(tau,\cdot)) exp(\int_tau^t Lip(v(s,\cdot))ds) dtau) and replace L_0/2 and 1+L_0/2 by the resulting dimension-free but larger constants.
issues.overall_effect: The quantitative guarantee Lip(w(\cdot;0,1)) <= L_0/2 and hence Lip(T(\cdot;y_obs)) <= 1+L_0/2 in cor:exists_lipschitz_onestep and thm:lipschitz_onestep_main are unestablished; only global Lipschitzness with a worse, exponentially inflated constant survives.
issues.title: Averaged-velocity Lipschitz bound ignores stretching of the flow maps
